text:
ops-bot: :rotating_light: alert fired: spot_avail_jitter | region=us-west1 | pool=gpu-mix | jitter_score=0.28 | threshold=0.2

alec: Saw it. Jitter spikes around 14:02-14:05 UTC, looks like repeated short drops rather than one sustained outage.

maria: Jitter_score? new composite? What's included?

sylvia: Quick explainer: jitter_score = interruption_rate * dip_duration_weight + dip_entropy. It penalizes frequent short dips more than a single long reclaim. Helps us detect noisy reclaim patterns.

jonathan: Impact summary: 5-95p latency widened by ~400ms during the pattern, inference queue depth up ~12%. No customer pages yet but error budget burn up for a couple of small enterprise routes.

alec: We keep paging on 10m sustained loss, but paging for these 3min micro-dips is too noisy. We need: better smoothing, a lightweight local absorb (warm-spare), and priority-aware hedging.

maria: Proposal: three-tier response
- observe: 1-3m micro dips tracked as "jitter" (no page)
- absorb: auto-route low % traffic to warm_spare pool for high-priority customers when jitter_score > threshold
- escalate: page if 2x metrics hit across 10m or if enterprise SLO impacted

sylvia: Implementation notes:
- add jitter_score to dashboard and alert rules
- histogram of dip_count per 5m and per-hour
- add dip_entropy metric (how fragmented the drop is)

jonathan: Routing snippet for runtime (prototype):

```yaml
jitter_alert:
  eval_window: 5m
  metric: jitter_score
  threshold: 0.20
  require_consecutive: 2

policy:
  when: jitter_alert
  actions:
    - type: warm_spare_route
      fraction: 0.10
      priority_filter: [enterprise, gold]
    - type: progressive_hedge
      base_fraction: 0.05
      adapt_rate: 0.02  # increase by 2% per additional window
      max_fraction: 0.30
      fallback: ondemand
```

maria: Key differences from our previous hedge: adaptive increase instead of one-shot 20%. Priority filter ensures free-tier PLG traffic doesn't trigger cost spikes. Also warm_spare absorbs immediate latency hit cheaply.

alec: Warm_spare sizing rule suggestion: warm_spare_gpus = max(ceil(steady_gpu_capacity * 0.03), 4). Keep small, per-region. Warm spare should be quickly prewarmed to avoid cold-start latency.

finance-bot: Please tag all hedge events with cost_tag=spot-hedge and record estimated extra ondemand_minutes for ledger. We'll reconcile weekly.

sylvia: Runbook bullets to add under "spot jitter":
1) Confirm jitter_score > threshold and dip_entropy > 0.15
2) Check provider health page / scheduled maintenance
3) If require_consecutive windows satisfied -> enable warm_spare routing
4) Monitor latency & error budget for 10m. If enterprise route SLO breached -> escalate to provider support + page infra oncall
5) Record hedge tag for finance and annotate the dashboard

jonathan: Ops tasks: add require_consecutive guard in signal pipeline, implement adaptive_hedge controller, and a canary for warm_spare (start at 5% traffic). I'll stub metrics and a synthetic test showing graceful absorb.

alec: Instrumentation: label each dip with pool_id, region, model_family, priority_tier, and provider. We want to slice by model_family to see if some models trigger more reclaim noise.

maria: Dashboard UX: add a small timeline of hedges per-region with cost delta estimate and per-customer tag counts. Helpful for postmortems.

sylvia: Also add alert suppression for short maintenance windows: if provider_reported_maintenance=true then mute jitter alerts for that region.

alec: Action items:
- jonathan: adaptive_hedge + warm_spare canary (3 days)
- sylvia: dashboard + jitter metrics + runbook edits (EOD tomorrow)
- maria: billing tags + coordinate with finance (this sprint)
- alec: runtime flag to enable require_consecutive windows and priority filters (PR review)

ops-bot: note posted: proposal PR at https://internal.redwood/changes/2056789012 and runbook draft at https://internal.redwood/runbooks/spot-jitter

alec: Thanks team. If the pattern repeats in other regions we'll consider a global jitter policy with per-region cost caps. :thumbsup:
